long: This is the radio. Not a podcast, not a stream. Live FM, straight out of the air. And you can watch it.
This is Visual Radio. It shows you what the radio says. Every word, every voice, every song. Free, open source, and running entirely on your own PC.
c03a
It starts with a software defined radio. This little Airspy Mini doesn't play a station.
c03b
It samples a whole slice of the radio spectrum, six million times a second. From here on, everything is software.
c04a
Out of that slice, Visual Radio picks one station. On FM it demodulates the audio, and decodes RDS: the station name, and often the song that's playing.
c04b
Every station gets a pin on the dial and a card of its own, with its name and what it's playing right now.
Every fifteen seconds, Google's YAMNet sound classifier listens and decides: is this talking, or music? The whole page follows. Calm captions for talk. A stage for songs.

Presenters talk over jingles, and singers sing over a band. Demucs pulls the voice out of the mix, so the speech recognizer hears only the voice. And you can listen to it too. Just the voice. Or just the band.
c07a
Then Whisper, running on the graphics card, writes out every word, with its own timestamp. The playback is delayed, so each word lights up the moment you hear it.
c07b
When a new voice takes over, it gets its own colour.
c07c
This is a Dutch station. Set the language to English, and Whisper translates on the fly.
And when the music starts, Visual Radio finds out which song it is. From the station's own data, or by fingerprinting the sound itself. The album cover sets the colours.
Every genre gets its own stage, pulsing on the beat. No lyrics? You get a live visual instead.
All of this runs live, on one PC, faster than the radio itself. No cloud needed.
Open it on your phone, a tablet, or the TV in the kitchen.
Visual Radio is free and open source. The link is below. Star it, try it, and see what your radio says.
